_readme: T-177 price parity — ONE table, read by both doors.
`test_boundary_dual_path.py` and `boundary.test.ts` used to carry this table twice, hand-copied,
including the payload builders. Two copies of a parity table are not a parity test: the whole
point is to catch the two doors drifting apart, and a divergence introduced on one side alone
was simply edited into that side's copy — both suites stayed green while the doors disagreed.
Measured: the roster half of T-177 landed in `boundary.py` and not in `boundary.ts`, and both
tables went on asserting `no_list_price_carried: ok=true` for a payload the Python door had
started refusing whenever a roster was passed.
So the cases live here, as WIRE PAYLOADS rather than builder calls, and each suite loads this
file and drives its own door with it. Adding a case is one edit; a door that answers
differently from its peer is red on one side and cannot be quietly reconciled on the other.
Each case: `bid` is the payload, `list_prices`/`max_discount_pct` are the caller's roster and
cap (null = not passed), `ok`/`reasons` are the verdict BOTH doors must return with
`schema_invalid:` reasons filtered out — those name pydantic/ajv field paths, which are the one
part of the vocabulary the two implementations are not expected to spell identically.
`path` and `now` apply to every case; the trust snapshot is each suite's `make_snapshot_table()`
/ `makeSnapshotTable()`, which is why every bid names `store-1`.
T-306/T-307 — THE ABSENT ROSTER IS THE EMPTY ROSTER, and seven rows here were re-baselined
for it. `list_prices: null` used to mean 'abstain': the wall read the bid's own `list_price`
claim and said nothing when there was none. That made the argument a caller FORGETS more
permissive than the argument a caller passes empty, on the money path — measured, a bid
charging 15.00 for a product the exchange prices at 100.00 was `ok: true, reasons: []` with
the roster omitted and refused with the roster spelled `{}`. `no_list_price_carried` was the
row that pinned it, in both languages. Every null-roster row now carries the refusals the
empty roster always carried, `an_empty_roster_answers_exactly_as_an_absent_one` holds the two
spellings against each other, and the two `a_call_wide_ceiling_...` rows pin T-307: a
`max_discount_pct` supplied without a roster is READ, in both directions, so a ceiling of 0
refuses a declared 20% and a ceiling of 20 does not.
Two rows kept their verdicts and gained a roster instead — `honest_price` and
`total_under_the_stated_unit_price`. Both are named for something only a caller that CAN
price the product ever reaches (an admission, and the total relation, which runs only at a
non-zero authorized depth); left on a null roster they would have gone on passing while
measuring `list_price_unavailable` instead of their own subject.
THE FLOOR (T-278). The `below_price_floor` rows at the end of this table are the gate for the
T-250 fix. That fix replaced an exact `price == 0` equality with a threshold — the floor is
`max(list_price * 0.001, 0.01)` — because an equality against zero has exactly one satisfying
value, so 0.001 for a product the roster prices at 100.00 was refused by nothing. The Python
half of the fix was verified through the exchange; the TypeScript half shipped with no case in
this table at all, and deleting `boundary.ts`'s floor block outright left all 806 vitest tests
green. These rows are what makes that a red suite instead. Both boundary directions are pinned
— a price exactly AT the floor is ADMITTED — because a wall that is closed rather than
fail-closed is its own defect, and the two halves of the `max` are pinned separately, on a
100.00 listing and on a 0.50 one, since either half alone admits what the other refuses.

cases.name: charges_under_the_carried_list_price
cases.why: the bid states its own list price and then charges 85% off behind a 20% declaration. The two `price_unreconcilable` reasons are T-306's: a caller passing no roster is told it cannot price what it admits, and cannot authorize the depth either. The original `price_under_declared_depth` still fires and still comes from the CARRIED claim — nothing here supplied a list price but the bid — so this row still pins WHERE the list price is read from. It no longer pins the DEPTH half: with no roster `authorized` is 0, so 15.00 is refused against the full 100.00, exactly as an honest 80.00 would be, and the row cannot tell whether the declared 20% was honoured at all. `a_carried_claim_is_measured_against_the_full_list_price_with_no_roster` is what carries that now — it charges 85.00, which the two bounds disagree about

cases.name: total_under_the_stated_unit_price
cases.why: a 20% discount off a stated 100.00 cannot produce a total of 15.00 under any reading of `total_price`. THE ROSTER IS NEW HERE AND THE VERDICT IS NOT (T-306): this relation runs only at a NON-ZERO authorized depth, and after T-306 an absent roster authorizes zero, so the row was measuring `list_price_unavailable` instead of the total relation it is named for. The roster agrees with nothing the bid says; it restores the row's subject

cases.name: amount_discount
cases.why: an amount off cannot be compared with a price without re-deriving what the offer means

cases.name: depth_out_of_range
cases.why: 150% off is not a depth this boundary can reconcile

cases.name: ambiguous_list_price
cases.why: two list_price claims naming different numbers: the bid does not get to pick which wall it is measured against. The `ambiguous_list_price` refusal is unchanged; the two around it are T-306's, because this caller passes no roster

cases.name: unreadable_list_price
cases.why: a bid does not get to disable the wall by making its own evidence unreadable. The `unreadable_list_price` refusal is unchanged; the two around it are T-306's, because this caller passes no roster

cases.name: honest_price
cases.why: 20% off a carried 100.00 is 80.00, and the bid charges exactly that — the positive control for this whole table, since a door that refused everything would satisfy every rejection row in it. THE ROSTER IS NEW HERE AND THE VERDICT IS NOT (T-306): an absent roster is now the empty roster, which refuses every bid for `list_price_unavailable`, so the admission this row exists to pin is only reachable from a caller that can price the product. The roster AGREES with the carried claim at 100.00, so nothing about the arithmetic changed

cases.name: no_list_price_carried
cases.why: THE ROW THAT ENCODED THE DEFECT, re-baselined by T-306. It read `ok: true, reasons: []` for a bid declaring 20%, charging 15.00 and carrying no list_price claim — the abstention, pinned in both languages. It was not a requirement: the identical call with `list_prices: {}` was refused, so the argument nobody passed was the permissive one, on the money path. The bid is untouched; only the verdict it earns has changed, and it now says what the wall actually knows — this caller cannot price the product and cannot authorize the depth

cases.name: roster_catches_the_bid_that_stayed_silent
cases.why: the same silent bid as above, now measured against the exchange's own list price

cases.name: roster_admits_the_honest_price
cases.why: a wall that refuses everything is not a wall

cases.name: roster_cannot_price_the_product
cases.why: a roster is evidence: a product it cannot price is an unavailable read, not a licence to fall back to the abstention

cases.name: roster_list_price_unreadable
cases.why: a row that is not a non-negative finite number

cases.name: carried_list_price_contradicts_the_roster
cases.why: inflate the stated list price until 15.00 looks like 20% off — the move after the first

cases.name: declared_depth_over_the_authorized_cap
cases.why: T-177's asymmetry: writing 85 instead of 20 used to price 15.00 out fine

cases.name: free_item_at_a_declared_hundred_percent
cases.why: 100% off is a depth like any other, and it is the one that costs the most

cases.name: depth_exactly_at_the_authorized_cap
cases.why: authorize_discount grants AT max_discount_pct and denies above it; both walls must agree about that boundary

cases.name: roster_that_authorizes_no_depth_refuses_a_discount
cases.why: a cap that can be omitted is a cap an attacker omits: unknown fails closed at zero

cases.name: roster_that_authorizes_no_depth_still_admits_a_list_price_bid
cases.why: a zero depth authorizes itself, so the cap is never consulted for one

cases.name: a_call_wide_cap_is_the_same_authority_as_a_row_one
cases.why: for a caller holding one approved number rather than a per-product column

cases.name: an_unreadable_cap_is_not_an_unbounded_one
cases.why: '20' is a string a seller wrote, not a depth

cases.name: free_item_at_a_cap_that_authorizes_everything
cases.why: the cap arrives on an unauthenticated request body, so `max_discount_pct: 100` is a free item every other relation in the walk calls arithmetically perfect

cases.name: a_silent_zero_is_a_free_item_too
cases.why: the same free item with the `discount` block deleted — the spelling that used to walk past the exchange because nothing was declared to judge

cases.name: a_zero_total_behind_a_list_price_unit
cases.why: a 100.00 unit with a 0.00 total is the free item wearing the other field

cases.name: a_silent_undercut_past_the_authorized_cap
cases.why: 15.00 for a 100.00 product under a 20% authorization is an 85% discount however the paperwork is spelled; an undeclared depth is measured against the cap like a declared one

cases.name: a_silent_price_exactly_at_the_authorized_cap
cases.why: the paired control: 80.00 IS the 20% the roster authorizes, and a store that files no paperwork for it must still be admitted or the wall is closed rather than fail-closed

cases.name: a_roster_that_prices_a_product_at_zero_has_no_free_item
cases.why: the floor is a comparison against the roster, not a rule that prices must be positive

cases.name: a_zero_price_with_no_roster_is_refused_by_the_roster_it_lacks
cases.why: an offer of 0.00 declaring no discount at all. The FLOOR is still dead code here and that is still the point of the row — the floor keys off `rostered`, never off a carried claim, so with no roster it cannot fire and the refusal below is not it. What changed under T-306 is one layer up: the caller that cannot price the product is refused for that, which is why this row is no longer named `..._is_unchanged`

cases.name: a_thousandth_of_a_dollar_is_below_the_proportional_floor
cases.why: T-250's exact defect, and the one the TypeScript door had NO gate for: 0.001 for a product the roster prices at 100.00. Every other relation in the walk is satisfied — the row authorizes 100%, so `listed * (100 - 100) / 100` is 0.00 and the price clears it — and the floor is the only thing left that objects. Written `=== 0` it objected to exactly one value and this one walked through.

cases.name: a_nanodollar_is_below_the_floor_by_nine_orders_of_magnitude
cases.why: the same walk-through one keystroke further from zero. 1e-09 is nine orders of magnitude under the smallest coin there is, and an equality against zero admits it just as readily as 0.001 — which is why the floor is a threshold and not a value.

cases.name: a_half_cent_is_below_the_absolute_floor_on_a_cheap_product
cases.why: the ABSOLUTE half of the floor, which the proportional half alone would miss: 0.1% of a 0.50 product is 0.0005, and 0.005 clears that comfortably while still being half a cent — an amount no settlement rail moves. `max(proportional, 0.01)` is what makes the wall bite on a cheap listing.

cases.name: a_price_exactly_at_the_proportional_floor_is_admitted
cases.why: the boundary value, and the direction the wall is likelier to fail: `<` not `<=`. 0.10 is exactly `100.00 * 0.001` in both languages' float arithmetic, so a door that refused it would be refusing the lowest price the contract still calls a price — closed rather than fail-closed.

cases.name: a_price_exactly_at_the_absolute_floor_is_admitted
cases.why: the same boundary on the other half of the `max`. One minor currency unit on a 0.50 listing is admitted; the half cent above is not. Both sides of `0.01` are pinned so the absolute half cannot be widened or dropped without a red row.

cases.name: a_price_a_cent_above_the_proportional_floor_is_admitted
cases.why: the positive control one step outside the wall. A floor that swallowed 0.11 on a 100.00 listing would be a different, wider rule than the one the constants state.

cases.name: a_total_below_the_floor_behind_a_list_price_unit
cases.why: the floor runs on both money fields independently. A 100.00 unit with a 0.001 total is the same undercut wearing the other field, and only the total collects a reason — one bad number reported once, at the site that carries it.

cases.name: a_silent_thousandth_on_a_row_that_authorizes_nothing
cases.why: the floor and the depth relation are different objections and a bid can collect both: 0.001 with no discount declared, on a row that states a list price and authorizes no depth at all, is below the floor AND below the full list price.

cases.name: an_undeclared_dollar_on_an_uncapped_hundred_clears_the_floor
cases.why: the CEILING on `PRICE_FLOOR_FRACTION`, restated at the boundary. The exchange's frozen `test_r10_still_admits_an_undeclared_undercut_where_nothing_is_authorized` pins 1.00 on a 100.00 row listing no cap as ADMITTED, so any floor at or above 1.00 there breaks a standing assertion. 0.1% leaves an order of magnitude of margin, and this row is the assertion that the margin is still there: 1.00 never collects a floor reason.

cases.name: an_undeclared_dollar_on_a_capped_hundred_is_refused_by_depth_not_by_the_floor
cases.why: the other row fixture, and the distinction a previous pass of this work got wrong. The exchange's sibling test refuses 1.00 on a CAPPED 100.00 row — but by the depth relation, not by the floor. 1.00 is above `price_floor(100.0)` on both rows; what differs is what the row authorizes. If a floor reason ever appears here, the wall has grown past the ceiling the frozen R10 case pins.

cases.name: an_empty_roster_answers_exactly_as_an_absent_one
cases.why: T-306's property, as a corpus row rather than a claim in a docstring. This is the `no_list_price_carried` payload with `list_prices: {}` instead of null, and the two rows must carry byte-identical reason lists: omission is the call a caller makes by FORGETTING, so it may never be the permissive one

cases.name: a_call_wide_ceiling_of_zero_binds_with_no_roster
cases.why: T-307. `max_discount_pct: 0` is a caller saying 'I authorize no discount at all', and it used to be dropped on the floor in silence whenever the roster was absent — the early return sat BEFORE the ceiling was read. The `discount_over_authorized_depth` reason is the whole assertion: it can only appear if the ceiling was consulted

cases.name: a_call_wide_ceiling_that_covers_the_declared_depth_with_no_roster
cases.why: T-307's other direction, and the one that stops the row above from passing for the wrong reason: the SAME bid under a ceiling of 20 earns no `discount_over_authorized_depth`, because 20% declared against 20% authorized is authorized. A ceiling that is never read would answer identically to both, so the pair distinguishes 'read and satisfied' from 'not read'. The bid is still refused — there is no list price to measure 15.00 against — which is T-306, not T-307

cases.name: a_carried_claim_is_measured_against_the_full_list_price_with_no_roster
cases.why: T-337's THIRD SITE, and the only row in this table that can see it. The other two sites of the T-306 repair are `authorizedDepth` and `rosterListPrice`; the third is the `authorized` fallback in `priceReasonsFor` / `_price_reasons`, which used to read `authorized = listPrices === undefined ? depth : 0` and so handed the offer its OWN declared depth back as its bound whenever the roster was absent — the self-granting cap the whole walk exists to end. Every other no-roster row in this table is blind to it, because they all charge far enough under list to be refused at BOTH bounds: `charges_under_the_carried_list_price` charges 15.00, which is under 100.00 and under 80.00 alike, so the verdict is identical either way. This row sits BETWEEN the two bounds on purpose — a carried list price of 100.00, a declared 20%, charging 85.00. Against the full list price (authorized 0, correct) 85.00 is an undercut and is REFUSED; against the depth the offer granted itself (authorized 20) the bound is 80.00 and 85.00 is ADMITTED. Measured: restoring that one ternary in `boundary.ts` left all 867 vitest tests and all 55 corpus rows green, so the divergence this corpus exists to prevent was invisible to it in exactly the place it matters most

cases.name: a_call_wide_ceiling_is_read_at_a_zero_declared_depth_with_no_roster
cases.why: THE FOURTH SITE. `_price_reasons` / `priceReasonsFor` reads the cap twice — once for a declared depth and once, in the `else`, for a declared ZERO — and the T-306 repair had to remove a `list_prices is not None` / `listPrices !== undefined` guard from BOTH. A per-site mutation sweep found the zero-depth one ungraded in both languages: reverting it alone left 910 pytest and 173 vitest green. Nothing else in this table can see it, because the two behaviours only diverge when a caller supplies a call-wide `max_discount_pct`, supplies NO roster, and meets an offer declaring no discount at all — every other row misses at least one of the three. Here the offer declares 0%, carries a list price of 100.00 and charges 85.00 under a ceiling of 20: reading the ceiling authorizes 20, the bound is 80.00 and 85.00 clears it, so the ONLY reason is the missing roster. Not reading it leaves `authorized` at zero, measures 85.00 against the full 100.00 and adds `price_under_declared_depth:offer.unit_price` — so the absence of that reason is the whole assertion. Note the direction: this mutant is stricter, not looser. It refuses an honest bid rather than admitting a dishonest one, which is the closed-rather-than-fail-closed defect this walk names elsewhere, and it is still a divergence between the two doors
